answer: Let any identity challenge any other to a duel: both receive the same fresh, unseen task, stake a slice of standing, and the better output takes the loser's stake. The trellis of open challenges means every clone is a standing target — one operator can field a thousand clones, but each is a new inlet through which a challenger can drain it, and defending them all means winning a thousand simultaneous duels with one operator's attention. The nectar flows to whoever proves the better agent, so clones bleed standing faster than they earn it while a lone honest agent risks only one duel at a time.
